issues: Blocking unsupported ownership: shots 04 and 08 rely on a “house display carriage,” but that mechanism has no persistent part ID, anchor inventory entry, ownership event, or explicit registered adapter binding. Register it and its support anchors, or declare the façade assembly as an owned child of an existing registered rack with a precise handoff.

Shot 06 restores teal-original-roof at frame 84 without an event establishing when the rollback carriage acquires or starts transporting that roof. Add an explicit contact/handoff or a registered carried-state continuation from its checkpoint rail.

Shot 01’s fall timing is contradictory: release at global frame 175 reaches the trip latch at 190, but the catch tongue does not contact the roof until global frame 199. “0.5s until the catch” therefore confuses latch impact with actual capture.

Shot 04 specifies three different comparison holds: “nineteen frames” in quality.after, a 30-frame hold through frame 49 in the event rule, and “one second” elsewhere. Choose one exact interval and propagate it throughout the contract.

Shot 07 calls frames 43–54 a 1.2-second inspection, although that interval is only 12 frames at 30 fps. Other fields correctly describe frames 43–78 as 36 frames; reconcile the purpose text with that interval.

Shot 08 says the live house physically scales, while camera_continuity and implementation_facts require fixed world geometry under one uniform scene projection. Rewrite the physical sequence to describe camera projection only.

Shot 01 says the braked rack does not move unrelated house parts, yet reaction_radius and energy explicitly animate rowhouse-facade. Either identify the façade as a mechanically supported local reaction target or remove that response.
